name: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree III
description:
You are given two nodes of a binary tree `p` and `q`, return their lowest common ancestor (LCA). Each node will have a reference to its parent node. The definition for `Node` is below: ```java class Node { public int val; public Node left; public Node right; public Node parent; } ``` According to the **[definition of LCA on Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lowest_common_ancestor)**: "The lowest common ancestor of two nodes p and q in a tree T is the lowest node that has both p and q as descendants (where we allow **a node to be a descendant of itself**)." **Example 1:** ![](https://imagedelivery.net/CLfkmk9Wzy8_9HRyug4EVA/8fa146da-6de4-4875-2b52-6f484cc30900/public) ```java Input: root = [5,3,4,2,1], p = 1, q = 2 Output: 3 ``` **Example 2:** ![](https://imagedelivery.net/CLfkmk9Wzy8_9HRyug4EVA/f7f41bbd-dd20-4445-1b27-320a7f5c6400/public) ```java Input: root = [5,3,4,2,1,null,9,null,11,10,12], p = 3, q = 12 Output: 3 ``` **Constraints:** * `2 <= The number of nodes in the tree <= 100,000`. * `-1,000,000,000 <= Node.val <= 1,000,000,000` * All `Node.val` are **unique**. * `p != q` * `p` and `q` will both exist in the tree.
